_doc: Stand-ins for the plugins a house fixture can list (scripts/eval_capabilities.py).
The real plugins live in their own repos; a stand-in carries only what core
reads from an installed plugin: its feature label and example phrase (the
'what can you do' answer), its tool (the router's list), its capability seams
(a weather plugin makes core's weather step aside) and APPROXIMATE fast paths.
A stand-in's reply is a marker ('[stand-in: the X feature handled this]'):
it says the plugin took the turn, never what the real plugin would say.
feature   - the feature name a reply may use (never the plugin's own name)
names     - extra words a reply must not say (global no-plugin-names check)
fast_paths  - regexes, or {pattern, uses_ai}: uses_ai marks a path the real plugin
answers with the model, so with AI off the stand-in can't speak for it
status in a house: ok (works), error (its service is missing: the stand-in
can't speak for the plugin, the case reports 'needs plugin'),
crash (its handler raises, as a broken plugin would)
